'ruled from 20 AD to 50 AD' as a client king of the Roman Empire; 'the Kingdom of Vannius (regnum Vannianum)', 'the first political unit in the area that is now Slovakia'. The Quadi page puts it a little earlier, after Maroboduus's fall: 'a Quadian named Vannius was made king' of the Marcomanni exiles, 'between the Morava and the Cusus rivers' (c. 18 AD there). ledger.note: 20: the Quadi kingdom of Vannius is a client of Rome. Vannius page: 'Vannius was a client king of the Roman Empire and ruled from 20 AD to 50 AD'; Quadi page: after his fall in 50/51 Vangio and Sido 'divided his realm between themselves as loyal Roman client kings', and the Quadi 'had a relatively stable relationship with the Romans as a client state during this period'. The Vannius page does not say that Rome installed him (it has him rising after Vibilius defeated Catualda). The region is the quadi_20 shape; the roman-empire dossier should carry the mirror (vassal_start, counterpart quadi, 20). ledger.note: 50: Vannius is deposed. 'Vibilius and the Hermunduri, with the Lugii, deposed Vannius' in 50/51 (Quadi page); the Vannius page: 'Vannius was easily defeated by the Lugii and the Hermunduri' and 'was awarded lands in Pannonia by Claudius'.

50/51: Vangio and Sido divide the realm. 'His nephews Vangio and Sido divided his realm "as loyal Roman client kings"'; Vannius page: 'subsequently divided between his nephews Vangio and Sido'. The state and its land continue under the nephews.

ledger.note: 173: the Quadi turn on Rome. 'By 173, the Romans began to turn on the Quadi, who had violated their treaty'; the Quadi page: they 'had expelled their Roman-approved king Furtius' by 173. In 171 the Quadi had 'agreed to leave their coalition' and returned 13,000 prisoners; in 174 they were 'subdued and compelled to provide hostages, auxiliary troops, and accept Roman garrisons'.

ledger.note: about 409: the Quadi leave their homeland. Jerome's 409 letter lists the Quadi first among the peoples occupying Gaul, and 'scholars consider the Quadi likely to have been prominent among the Suevi who founded the kingdom in Gallaecia'; Jerome had listed them among peoples ravaging the provinces after 395. The page does not say who took the Morava lands; the dissolve is a bridge. [Fix pass 2026-10-19: the Kingdom of the Suebi page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_the_Suebi) was opened for the end of the homeland and does not say the Quadi left the Danube: it dates the Rhine crossing to the night of 31 December 405 and notes that Jerome's 409 letter 'lists the Quadi and not the Suevi' while Orosius places the Suevi in 406; it adds that other Suevi groups were residing by the Danube in the 5th and 6th centuries. 409 stays a conf-1 bridge.]

wars.name: Marcomannic Wars

zones.text: 'near the Morava river in southwestern Slovakia, southern Moravia, and northeastern Lower Austria' (Lower Austria not drawn)

wars.outcome: Roman victory, status quo ante bellum: the Quadi left the coalition in 171, rebelled in 173 and again in 177, accepted Roman garrisons in 174, and were beaten at Laugaricio (179); Commodus made peace in 180.
wars.note: Quadi page: 'In 179 Rome won a decisive battle at Laugaricio'.

wars.name: Campaigns of Carinus and Numerian against the Quadi
wars.outcome: 'Carinus and Numerian held campaigns against the Quadi in 283-284'; the Quadi were 'again listed among attackers in 285'. No territorial change.
wars.note: Caracalla had had the Quadi king Gaiobomarus executed in 214/215.

wars.name: Constantius II's Danube campaign against the Quadi
wars.outcome: Constantius II crossed the Danube; Vitrodorus, son of King Viduarius (probably of the western Quadi), swore loyalty to Rome.

wars.name: Quadi and Sarmatian invasion of Illyricum
wars.outcome: A Roman general murdered King Gabinius at dinner in 374 over a fort; 'the Quadi, who had long been quiet, were suddenly aroused to an outbreak'; the Germanic Wars page has the Quadi and Sarmatians invading former Illyricum in 374. No territorial change.
wars.note: The Quadi page does not date Valentinian I's death, so 375 is not supported by it.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks. Three pages opened. The homeland is the Quadi page's 'initially' description (undated) drawn as Jihomoravsky, Bratislavsky, Trnavsky and Nitriansky; northeastern Lower Austria is left out (Niederosterreich is a whole Austrian state, too large), and the later eastward extension to Vac is not drawn. The pages date neither the Quadi's arrival nor their departure; 409 is the date of Jerome's letter. No capital, no rulers drawn (kings named: Vannius 20-50, Vangio and Sido from 50/51, Furtius 173, Gaiobomarus executed 214/215, Viduarius c. 357, Gabinius murdered 374). The Quadi page puts Vannius's elevation c. 18 AD, the Vannius page 20 AD, the Marcomanni page 19 AD; 20 is used. Wikidata id unknown. The marcomanni dossier records the matching 'gain' of Moravia (counterpart quadi) in 19, to be aligned to 20 by the gap-filler or reviewer. Counterparts that need dossiers: 'Hermunduri', 'Lugii', 'sarmatians' (exists, af/eu-04 batch).
